title: Immunoglobulin G preparation from plasma samples and analysis of its affinity kinetic binding to peptide hormones
protocol: Collect blood samples in lithium heparin tubes containing 3 μL of protease cocktail inhibitor or use aprotinin tubes.
Centrifuge the blood sample at 3000 rpm for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Collect the plasma and acidify it with HCl 1N to prevent peptide degradation, using 10% of the plasma volume.
Add 1 ml of acetonitrile 60% in TFA 1% to Strata® C18-SEP columns and centrifuge at 3000 rpm for 3 minutes at 4°C to activate the column.
Wash the column three times with 3 ml of TFA 1%.
Dilute plasma at half with TFA 1% (500 μL plasma and 500 μL TFA 1%), load it onto the activated Strata® C18-SEP column, and centrifuge to separate peptides from IgG.
Store the effluent containing proteins at -80°C for further purification of IgG or elute peptides with acetonitrile 60% in TFA 1% for concentration assay.
Wash the column twice more with 3 ml of TFA 1%.
Evaporate the eluent under vacuum to eliminate maximum acetonitrile.
Freeze and lyophilize the eluent for 72 hours to purify peptides.
Resuspend peptide fraction in PBS and quantify purified peptides using appropriate kits.
Add 500 μL Melon Gel purification support to mini spin columns.
Centrifuge at 5000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Wash twice with 300 μL purification buffer and centrifuge at 5000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Dilute effluent-containing IgG from previous step at one-quarter with purification buffer (1 mL effluent and 3 mL purification buffer).
Add 500 μL of diluted sample to the column and incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature on a roller mixer.
Centrifuge at 5000 rpm for 30 seconds to purify IgG.
Repeat steps adding 500 μL of diluted sample, incubating for 5 minutes, and centrifuging until all diluted sample is passed through the column.
Pool the entire fraction obtained in a hemolysis tube for freezing and lyophilization over 72 hours.
After lyophilization, resuspend purified IgG with a volume of BIAcore HBS-EP buffer corresponding to the plasma volume at the beginning of the experiment.
Determine the concentration of IgG using a nanodrop or similar device.
Open the BIAcore control software and place a new CM5 chip in the BIAcore or one with a free flowcell (command → undock → change the chip → dock → prime to wash the chip).
Mix 100 μL of NHS and 100 μL of EDC and place the tube in position R2A1 in the BIAcore.
Dilute the peptide in acetate buffer at a concentration of 0.5 mg/mL and place the tube in R2A2 position, ensuring an ideal volume of 200 μL for repeated injections during coating.
Place 200 μL of ethanolamine in the R2A3 position.
Place a complete vial of NaOH 10 mM in the R2F3 position.
Start a new sensorgram by selecting the flowcell and setting the flow rate to 5 µL/min.
Activate the flowcell using an injection of NHS/EDC mix at 35 μL from position R2A1.
Inject peptide onto the chip using a volume of 35 μL from position R2A2, repeating if necessary.
Fix the peptide on the chip with ethanolamine injected in 35 μL volume from position R2A3.
Regenerate the chip once or twice with NaOH 10 mM at a volume of 10 µL from position R2F3.
Stop the sensorgram and save it.
Dilute IgG using HBS-EP buffer for affinity kinetics determination.
Place 3360 nM IgG in R2A6, 1680 nM in R2A5, 840 nM twice (R2A4 and R2A7), 420 nM in R2A3, and 210 nM in R2A2.
Place a blank HBS-EP buffer in both R2A1 and R2A9 for blanks.
Run the multi-cycle kinetic program.
Wash the system with HBS-EP buffer.
Insert the sample into the BIAcore and click continue.
Start the program with 2 baseline runs using HBS-EP buffer to derive the signal.
Save a sensorgram for each concentration.
Analyze results using BIAevaluation software.
Open the file corresponding to the sample for analysis.
Select the first and second curves corresponding to the 2 startup runs to check similarity.
Keep one blank curve for analysis.
Delete extreme parts of the curves from 0 to 80 seconds.
Cut sections from 535 to 900 seconds.
Remove artifact peaks that interact with the analysis.
Line up all remaining curves to 0.
Select a part at the beginning in the linear region for Y-transformation.
Transform the selected area to 0 at the average of the selection.
Replace curves with transformed data.
Subtract the blank curve from the others.
Fit the curves to obtain kinetic parameters using the simultaneous ka/kd Langmuir binding model 1:1.
Copy the table data to Excel for statistical analysis.
